analysis.title: ExxonMobil Corp. 3Q26 Review: Beat driven by refining, long-term project backlog is building
key_insights: XOM 3Q26 adjusted EPS was $4.23/sh vs BofA and Street estimates of $4.13. Adjusted earnings were $17,505mn vs BofA estimate $17,083mn and consensus $17,000mn.

The beat came mainly from refining: throughput ran at 91% utilization and refining capture was ahead of expectations. Support came from XOM's highest global diesel yield and North American diesel volumes, and optimized maintenance despite downtime at the Joliet refinery and disrupted refining in the Middle East and Asia.

Energy Products earnings were $9,053mn vs BofA $8,487mn (+7%). Upstream earnings were $7,308mn vs BofA $7,436mn (-2%). Specialty Products were $1,283mn vs BofA $1,451mn (-12%). Chemical Products were $725mn vs BofA $647mn (+12%).
Free cash flow was in line with expectations at $16.5bn on in-line capex of $7bn. Buybacks were flat at $5bn per quarter, so excess cash went to debt paydown (change in debt -$7,497mn).

YTD net debt is down $11bn, lowering net debt to capital to 7.5%, which BofA calls peer-leading. XOM raised its dividend 4% in the quarter and announced plans for another $20bn of buybacks in 2027, in line with 2026.
Advantaged asset production is on track to reach 65% of total volumes by 2030 (58% YTD). Structural cost reductions rose $0.6bn QoQ to $16.9bn.

CEO Darren Woods said on the call that refining cracks might not return to normalized levels until after 2027. BofA reads this as supporting the risk/reward of incremental brownfield refinery expansions.

XOM is high-grading its downstream assets toward scale refineries that make higher-value products, which has raised diesel yields by 3.5% since 2019. The $2bn Beaumont expansion (+250kbd in 2023) achieved a three-year payback. The USGC asset reconfiguration (2028-2030) is expected to add another 100kbd of distillate capacity.
FY26 production guidance was held flat at 1.8mbd. BofA says Guyana has significant potential in 2030+, and Permian advancements and efficiencies could drive upside to the 2030 guidance.

In LNG, XOM announced asset swaps to secure operatorship of PNG LNG and Rovuma LNG. Rovuma LNG is still expected to reach FID in 2026. Golden Pass train 2 is expected to be mechanically complete before YE26 and Train 3 by mid-2027.

BofA reiterates a Neutral rating with a $181 price objective vs the $183.29 share price. The PO rests on a SOTP of segment DCFs through 2050, discounted at a 7.4% WACC, with long-term Brent at $70/bbl.

market_movers.rationale: BofA reiterates Neutral after the 3Q26 beat driven by refining. The $181 PO sits slightly below the $183.29 price, with the share price near the 52-week high of $184.88.

sector_views.rationale: BofA stays Neutral on XOM. Refining margins and downstream investment support earnings, but the stock trades near its PO and 52-week high.

earnings_insights: XOM 3Q26 reported adjusted EPS $4.23 vs BofA/consensus estimate $4.13 (+3%). Adjusted earnings were $17,505mn vs BofA estimate $17,083mn and consensus $17,000mn (+2% vs BofA).

3Q26 segment earnings (reported vs BofA estimate): Upstream $7,308mn vs $7,436mn, Energy Products $9,053mn vs $8,487mn, Chemical Products $725mn vs $647mn, Specialty Products $1,283mn vs $1,451mn, Corp & Other -$864mn vs -$938mn.
3Q26 refining throughput was 3,735 (table units) vs BofA estimate 3,694 and consensus 3,709. US throughput was 1,941 vs BofA 1,827 (+6%), international 1,794 vs 1,867 (-4%).
3Q26 total upstream production was 4,496 MBOED vs BofA estimate 4,440 and consensus 4,458. Liquids were 3,279 MBD vs BofA 3,287. Natural gas was 7,301 MMCFD vs BofA 6,920 (+5%).
3Q26 realizations: liquids $84.42/bbl vs BofA $83.22. Natural gas $7.84/mcfe vs BofA $8.45 (-7%), with international gas at $13.92 vs BofA $17.10.

3Q26 CFO ex working capital (ex asset sales) was $23,434mn vs BofA estimate $25,027mn (-6%). Cash capex was $7,002mn vs BofA $7,410mn. FCF ex working capital (ex asset sales) was $16,432mn vs BofA $17,617mn (-7%) and consensus $15,217mn.
3Q26 share buybacks were $5,103mn vs BofA and consensus $5,000mn.
FY26 production guidance held flat at 1.8mbd. XOM announced plans for $20bn of share repurchases in 2027, in line with 2026.

macro_indicators.interpretation: BofA's XOM price objective uses $70/bbl Brent as the long-term oil price in its SOTP valuation.

macro_indicators.reading: Might not return to normalized levels until after 2027
macro_indicators.interpretation: XOM's CEO said on the call that cracks may stay elevated for longer, which supports refining earnings and downstream expansion economics.

risk_factors: The report points to Joliet refinery downtime and impacted refining operations in the Middle East and Asia.
Upstream and specialty products earnings came in below expectations.
International natural gas realizations were well below BofA's estimate ($13.92 vs $17.10).
The BofA price objective basis and risk section is cut off in the text provided, so the report's listed risks are not available.
geopolitical: Refining operations in the Middle East and Asia were impacted during the quarter, per the report.
